hook: What happens when a waterfall hits twelve times its normal flow?

sections.voiceover: What happens when a waterfall hits twelve times its normal flow?
In October 2026, the Iguazú River surged to a record 17,700 cubic meters per second. Super El Niño rainfall triggers extreme water levels throughout the entire Iguazú River basin today.
But the 1.6 kilometer span of the falls between Brazil and Argentina faces dangerous conditions.
This massive surge forces water through the Iguazú Falls at twelve times the normal rate. National park officials in Argentina closed the Circuito Superior walkway to all tourists.
The Iguazú Falls reached a record flow of 17,700 cubic meters per second this October.
